title: Ovid's Metamorphoses
objective: After this level you can explain why Ovid's poem of transformations became the myth book later writers borrowed from.
summary: Ovid's Metamorphoses (about 8 CE) strings myths of transformation from creation to Julius Caesar. Its Daphne and Pyramus and Thisbe fed poets and painters for centuries, Shakespeare included.

cards.headline: A woman becomes a tree to escape a god. Ovid made sure we'd all hear of it.
cards.body: Daphne refused every suitor, Apollo included. When the god chased her, she prayed for rescue and became a laurel tree. Apollo claimed the laurel for poets and, in Rome, for triumphs. Her story is one of many in a single Roman poem.

cards.headline: A poem made of changes
cards.body: Ovid finished the Metamorphoses, 15 books of Latin hexameter verse, about 8 CE. It collects myths, many from Greek sources, and in each a transformation plays a part. They run in order from the creation of the world (chaos turned to order, the first change of all) to the death and deification of Julius Caesar. That same year, the emperor banished Ovid to Tomis.

cards.headline: Lovers, a wall and a mulberry
cards.body: Pyramus and Thisbe are Babylonian lovers forbidden to marry, who whisper through a crack in the wall between their houses. They plan to meet at a mulberry tree. Thisbe flees a lioness and drops her veil; Pyramus finds it, thinks she is dead and kills himself, and Thisbe follows. The transformation? The tree's snow-white berries are dyed dark purple by his blood.

cards.fact: For centuries, writers and painters borrowed from Ovid.
cards.context: Ovid gave scores of Greek legends the form later generations knew. From the 15th to the 17th centuries, it's hard to name a poet or painter of note who didn't owe him something. In Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, workmen act a farcical Pyramus and Thisbe, and the same tale was one inspiration for Romeo and Juliet.

questions.prompt: What ties together the stories in Ovid's Metamorphoses?

options.label: Each ends with a stated moral

questions.explanation: Metamorphoses means transformations: every story in it involves a change of form.

questions.prompt: Why did so many later poets and painters borrow from Ovid?

options.label: He invented every Greek myth himself
options.rationale: Many of his stories came from Greek sources.

options.label: His poem gave scores of Greek legends a lasting form
His was the only Latin poem to survive
Shakespeare translated his poem into English
options.rationale: Shakespeare borrowed from him; he did not translate him.

questions.explanation: Ovid gave scores of Greek legends their definitive form, so later writers and painters drew on his versions.
